justification: Standard: changes how the area check learns the council, which gates the whole answer (the four excluded councils). Not Minor: it adds a database-backed fallback and changes the live call's limits. Not Critical: the live service is still asked first and its answer (even 'no council') is never overridden, the fallback answers only when a lot contains the point or exactly one council is within about 100 m, and every failure leaves the answer at can't tell exactly as before.

pre_impl.existing_data: lot_search_index holds lga_name on 3,126,418 lots (128 distinct councils) with geom SRID 4326, a GiST index (idx_lsi_geom) and computed_at (2026-06-18). The four councils the law excludes appear under the same names the live service returns. The live state boundary service answered in 0.1-0.3 s when called alone but stalled in waves: in 8 bursts of the engine's real requests latency rose from 1 s to 7 s with six requests stalling together; on 2026-11-18 the council lookup failed 11 times in a row over about 4 minutes.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I first assumed the boundary service was simply slow. Measured, it is fast when idle and stalls intermittently on shared government servers; it could not be made to fail on demand.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Adds services/lmr_area_lga.py (one read-only lookup) and injects it from the API route, the same way flood_fn is injected, so lmr_area_inputs stays database-free. No rule, source, law figure or layer changes.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The copy is a snapshot (computed 2026-06-18); council boundaries rarely change and the answer says 'as at' the date whenever the copy is used. Live is asked first. Measured 2026-11-18 with the final rules: 60 of 60 random lot points returned that lot's council; 48 of 48 points shifted 30-60 m into roads in the four excluded councils returned the same council as the live service (0 wrong, 0 refused). No status flag exists on lot_search_index (it is built from the cadastre snapshot); a lot's council does not change when a lot is subdivided.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A - the API response gains an optional measured.lga_source and one note; no frontend change.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A wrong council could wrongly include or exclude one of the four excluded councils. Guarded by: the lot containing the point decides; otherwise only exactly one council within about 100 m counts (a road between councils or a border gives no answer); live first and never overridden; a missing council still gives can't tell. The review's wide-road case is pinned by a test and a deliberate break.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_area_lga.py tests/test_lmr_area_inputs.py tests/test_lmr_area_decision.py -q ; PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 DATABASE_URL=... python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_area_lga_real_db.py -o addopts= -m database
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The fallback accepts a border, swaps latitude and longitude, or replaces the live answer; or the decision drops the source note.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Deliberate breaks, each failing a named test: (A) accept a road between councils: test_an_excluded_council_is_never_lost_to_a_neighbour_across_a_wide_road (2 failed); (B) let the fallback override a live 'no council' answer: test_a_live_answer_of_no_council_is_never_overridden_by_the_fallback (1 failed); (C) ignore the containing lot: test_the_lot_the_point_is_in_decides_even_when_another_council_is_close (1 failed). Earlier round: accepting a border, swapping lat/lng and skipping live each failed a test. Restored: 65 passed (all area-check tests 168 passed). Real database plus live service: 3 passed (excluded councils resolve to themselves or nothing; 16 shifted points never differ from live; 20 random lots agree with live where both answer).

functions.name: lga_from_snapshot
functions.input: a latitude and longitude and an optional connection factory
functions.output: the council and the as-at date when exactly one council is within 40 m, else None
functions.if_none: None means no council, so the decision stays at can't tell; it never raises

functions.name: _get_json
functions.input: a url, parameters and optional timeout and attempts
functions.output: the parsed answer or None after the allowed tries
functions.if_none: None means the service did not answer; defaults stay 12 seconds and 2 tries

functions.name: _lga_resolved
functions.input: a point and an optional fallback function
functions.output: the council and a source marker, the marker empty when the live service answered
functions.if_none: no live answer and no usable fallback returns no council and no marker

functions.name: _lga_live
functions.input: a latitude and longitude for the live state boundary service
functions.output: a pair: whether the service answered, and the council it named or None
functions.if_none: an answer naming no council is returned as answered with no council, never replaced

values.value: council name (lga_name) and the copy's computed_at date for lots near the point
values.if_missing: no lot near, a border, or a database problem gives None and the decision says can't tell

queries.purpose: Which council owns the lot or lots within 40 m of this point
queries.where_clause: WHERE ST_DWithin(geom, point, 0.001) GROUP BY lga_name, with bool_or(ST_Intersects(geom, point)) marking a containing lot; read-only session, 3 s statement limit, uses idx_lsi_geom (about 150 ms including a fresh connection)

break_it.scenario: The point is on a road or wide reserve between two councils, or in an excluded council's road with only a neighbour's lots nearest.
break_it.what_happens: A guess could name the neighbour and mis-handle an excluded council.
break_it.how: A lot containing the point decides; otherwise exactly one council within about 100 m is needed, so a road between councils returns None. Pinned by tests and a deliberate break; 48 of 48 shifted real points matched the live service.

break_it.scenario: The live service answers but names no council (for example a point off the land).
break_it.what_happens: The fallback could override the authority and invent a council.
break_it.how: An answered-but-empty live result is returned as is and the fallback is never called; tested and broken on purpose.

break_it.scenario: The database is slow, down or unset when the live service is also failing.
break_it.what_happens: No council could be found at all.
break_it.how: 3 s connect and statement limits, any error returns None, and the result is the same can't tell as before this change.

break_it.scenario: A user reads an answer without knowing the council came from our copy, or is told the service timed out when it returned an error.
break_it.what_happens: Wrong assumption about the source or the cause.
break_it.how: measured.lga_source carries source and date; the note states the copy's date and says the service 'did not give an answer', never 'in time'.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after deploy call /pipeline/housing-sepp/area-check for a Penrith point and confirm measured.lga is PENRITH; the fallback only shows when the live service stalls, so confirm by the opt-in real database test.
